solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Commander’s leading question for German? (8)

indicators.note: COM goes in front of, leading, the question

blocks.note: Com. is the abbreviation for commander
a poser is a puzzling question

annotation.surface: An officer's first question about a German prisoner or visitor.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital hides the definition: Sir Edward German was an English composer of light opera, and the question mark admits he is only an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Edward German wrote comic operas such as Merrie England, so he is one composer.

entries.clue: More vino flowing? One will swallow anything that’s going (8)

definitions.text: One will swallow anything that’s going

indicators.note: letters that flow move freely into a new order

annotation.surface: A drinker asks for more wine, and someone who will drink anything obliges.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description rather than a dictionary one: an omnivore eats whatever food is available.
annotation.definitionFit: An omnivore eats plants and animals alike, swallowing whatever is going.

entries.clue: Formalities for device being used outside clubs (8)

indicators.note: TOOL is placed around, outside, the C

annotation.surface: Rules about how some gadget may be used around golf or card clubs.
annotation.walkthrough: "for" looks like a link to the definition, but it supplies PRO, and the club is the card suit.
annotation.definitionFit: Protocol is the set of formalities of official or diplomatic behaviour.

entries.clue: Put together ring for wrestling (4)

blocks.note: to sum is to add up, put together

annotation.surface: Assembling a ring in which a wrestling bout will take place.
annotation.walkthrough: The ring looks like the wrestling ring of the surface, but it only supplies the round letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain name-for-kind match: the answer is the traditional Japanese form of the sport named.

entries.clue: One growing tall is embarrassed to court daughter (7)

annotation.surface: A gangly adolescent blushes at the idea of asking a girl out.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes "One growing tall" a teenager; it is a tree.
annotation.definitionFit: The redwood grows taller than any other tree.

entries.clue: Flee island in confusion, giving up everything one loves? (4-6)

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into disorder

annotation.surface: Someone flees an island in a panic, leaving behind everything dear to them.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes giving everything up a forced loss in an escape; the definition means choosing to go without.
annotation.definitionFit: Self-denial is going without the things one wants; the question mark marks the exaggeration.

entries.clue: Dispute in law illuminated initially indistinct entry (8)

indicators.note: take only the first letter of indistinct

blocks.note: a gate is a way in

annotation.surface: A legal argument about a doorway that was poorly lit and hard to make out.
annotation.walkthrough: "Dispute" reads as a noun, but the definition is the verb phrase: to litigate is to dispute in law.
annotation.definitionFit: To litigate is to contest a matter in a court of law.

entries.clue: Yarmouth fisherman foolish to conceal source of cod? (8)

indicators.note: POTTY hides EGG inside it

blocks.note: a cod starts life as an egg

annotation.surface: A silly fisherman trying to keep secret where he catches his cod.
annotation.walkthrough: Dan Peggotty is the Great Yarmouth fisherman in Dickens’s David Copperfield; Yarmouth is a fishing port on England's east coast.
annotation.definitionFit: Daniel Peggotty in David Copperfield lives in an upturned boat at Yarmouth and fishes for a living.

entries.clue: What could be game that is interrupted by day when light fades (8)

indicators.note: to be interrupted is to have something break into your middle, so D goes between the I and E

blocks.note: a game could be one event in a sports meeting

annotation.surface: Wondering whether play will continue once the light goes.
annotation.walkthrough: "game" invites an adjective sense (willing); here it is a noun, one example of an event.
annotation.definitionFit: Eventide is an old word for evening, when the daylight fades.

entries.clue: Educated at home because of medical (8)

blocks.note: for = because of, as in 'famous for'
med = medical, as in med school

annotation.surface: A child home-schooled on health grounds.
annotation.walkthrough: "at home" belongs with "Educated" in the surface, but it is a separate piece: IN.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone informed is knowledgeable, educated about a subject.

entries.clue: Speaking at length with a fine cast (8)

blocks.note: F = fine, as on pencil leads
to fling is to cast, throw

annotation.surface: An actor holding forth among a splendid company of players.
annotation.walkthrough: "cast" suggests actors, and "fine" praise; both are single pieces of wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Waffling is talking at length without saying much.

entries.clue: Criterion for judging type of telephone that’s small inside (10)

indicators.note: the phone has something small inside it, so S goes within the phone's letters

blocks.note: a touch-tone phone dials by keypad tones
S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: Judging a phone by whether it is small inside.
annotation.walkthrough: A touch-tone telephone dials with keypad tones rather than a rotary dial.
annotation.definitionFit: A touchstone is a standard by which things are judged, from the stone once used to test gold.

entries.clue: Temporary sporting shoes including right and left I have (5-5)

indicators.note: SHOD takes in the other pieces

blocks.note: Rt = right, as in Rt Hon

annotation.surface: A pair of borrowed trainers, with a right and a left, for a while.
annotation.walkthrough: "sporting" looks like athletics but means wearing, so "sporting shoes" is SHOD.
annotation.definitionFit: Something short-lived lasts only a short time, so it is temporary.

entries.clue: Truth of account in newspaper (4)

indicators.note: an item in a paper is printed within it, so AC sits within FT

annotation.surface: Whether a newspaper report can be trusted.
annotation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, a British daily; "account" suggests a news report but gives only its abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a true thing, an established truth.

entries.clue: Creature one’s seen swimming round a large island (3,4)

indicators.note: the letters of ONES swim into a new order
to go round something is to encircle it, so the jumbled letters enclose A, L, I

annotation.surface: A swimmer seen circling a big island.
annotation.walkthrough: The creature does belong in the scene: sea lions swim round islands.
annotation.definitionFit: A sea lion is a creature, a large eared seal.

entries.clue: Relief once certain to include sad case (8)

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it as a part, so SURE holds the jumbled CASE
a sad case is in a sorry state, so its letters are in a mess

annotation.surface: Certain relief for a sad case, as it was once.
annotation.walkthrough: "once" marks the word as archaic: surcease is now mostly remembered from Poe's The Raven.
annotation.definitionFit: Surcease is an old word for cessation or relief, as in 'surcease of sorrow'.

entries.clue: Police dog mutilated assailant but a second’s escaped (8)

indicators.note: the letters are mangled into a new order
one S gets away from the fodder

blocks.note: S = second; one of the two S's is removed

annotation.surface: A police dog savages an attacker, but a moment later he gets away.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's 'a second' sounds like time; it is the letter S, and only one of ASSAILANT's two goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Alsatian is the British name for the German shepherd, a common police dog.

entries.clue: Passionate about quiet school’s location? (7)

indicators.note: about means around, so FIERY is placed around SH

annotation.surface: Someone passionate about a quiet location for a school.
annotation.walkthrough: The school is a school of fish, and a fishery is where they are found.
annotation.definitionFit: A fishery is a fishing ground, where schools of fish are.

entries.clue: Refusing to change what actor might have difficulty with (8)

definitions.text: what actor might have difficulty with

blocks.clueFragment: what actor might have difficulty with
blocks.note: read as two words: a piece of script that is tough to deliver

annotation.surface: A stubborn actor refuses to alter the line they struggle with.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition only works split as HARD LINE, a difficult line of dialogue.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the political adjective for an unbending stance, and a line in a script that is hard to say.

entries.clue: Verbal attack avoided by British by the way? (8)

indicators.note: B keeps away, leaving the rest

blocks.note: a broadside is a fierce verbal attack

annotation.surface: A British target dodging a tirade, mentioned in passing.
annotation.walkthrough: "by the way" pretends to be an aside, but read literally it means beside the road.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal reading: 'way' is an old word for road, so what lies by it is the verge.

entries.clue: Disturbing call in support of Indian government rising (7)

indicators.note: RAJ goes up the down entry, becoming JAR
RING sits under JAR, supporting it in a down clue

blocks.note: the Raj was British rule in India
to ring is to call on the phone

annotation.surface: An unsettling call to back India's government as it rises.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down entry, "in support of" means underneath, and "rising" means read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a jolting, grating effect unsettles, like a harsh noise.

entries.clue: Hives perhaps knocked over in Noah’s Ark (4)

indicators.note: the letters read backwards
the answer lies inside the words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words: noaHS ARk

annotation.surface: Beehives tipped over aboard Noah's Ark.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hives" suggests bees; here it is the skin complaint.
annotation.definitionFit: Hives is one kind of rash, hence 'perhaps'.

entries.clue: One dragging otter along? Alarm went right off (10)

indicators.note: the letters go off, bad, into a new order

annotation.surface: An alarm sounds as someone drags an otter along.
annotation.walkthrough: The otter is not the animal: an otter board keeps a trawl net open as it is dragged.
annotation.definitionFit: A trawlerman fishes with a trawl net, which is spread by otter boards.

entries.clue: Foreign cathedral city, one English ignored, French king overturned (8)

indicators.note: one E is left out of EXETER
ROI is turned over to IOR

blocks.note: Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon

annotation.surface: A cathedral city abroad, with its English visitor ignored and French king deposed.
annotation.walkthrough: "Foreign" looks like a description of the city; it is the definition, in the sense of external.
annotation.definitionFit: Exterior means outside, foreign to the thing itself.

entries.clue: Ejected well on time (4)

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring, a well

annotation.surface: Thrown out right on schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: "well" reads as an adverb; it is the noun, a spring of water, which a spa is.
annotation.definitionFit: Spat is the past tense of spit, to eject from the mouth.

entries.clue: Hinted at one politician getting sanctioned (8)

annotation.surface: Hints that an MP is about to be disciplined.
annotation.walkthrough: "sanctioned" reads as punished; here it means permitted.
annotation.definitionFit: What is implicit is implied, hinted at rather than stated.

entries.clue: Trinity College rascal’s topped record during term? (8)

indicators.note: ELPEE loses its top letter
what happens during a period sits within it, so the record goes within SPAN

blocks.note: a span is a term, a period of time
LP spelt out as a word

annotation.surface: A Trinity student rascal has broken a record during the term.
annotation.walkthrough: Trinity College is in Dublin, pointing to an Irish word. ELPEE is the dictionary spelling of LP.
annotation.definitionFit: Spalpeen is an Irish word for a rascal or good-for-nothing.

entries.clue: Fish around that location could be grouper (8)

indicators.note: to be around something is to surround it, so the fish's letters wrap THERE

blocks.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

annotation.surface: A fish swimming around a spot where there might be a grouper, another fish.
annotation.walkthrough: "grouper" is a fish, but here it means one who groups things, a gatherer.
annotation.definitionFit: A grouper, one who puts things in groups, could be called a gatherer.
